summary: Hold, and set depends_on to cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s2-finite-fix. Its valuable part, judging w13+silu and w2 independently with their own verdict lines, is merged into the finite-fix run. Its mixed Marlin/wgmma production path (bridge plus mismatched align blocks) should be minted as stage 3 only if that check shows exactly one kernel correct.
justification: The diagnostic idea is right. The stage 1b canary only checked `out`, so nobody knows whether w13+silu, w2, an unwritten cache3 row (torch.empty) or the norm produced the non-finite value. Judging each kernel against Marlin with Marlin-fed inputs answers that. As a separate run in parallel with finite-fix, though, it spends a second check on the same unfixed bug. Its own fix (3), smem zeroing and padding-row zero-fill, is a subset of finite-fix's. It explicitly excludes the descriptor/fragment/expect_tx fixes, so if the bug is in either GEMM's shared machinery (B descriptor, TMA swizzle, pipeline), both kernels fail here and the run measures nothing. WEAKEST LINK: the mixed production path. The wgmma path aligns at block 16 into sorted-slot h_sorted, while master's Marlin uses block_size_m 16 at bs=128 and 32 at bs=256 with route-indexed cache2. Mixing them needs either a second align or running Marlin at block 16, which detunes the incumbent row at bs=256 and confounds the M2 comparison. It also needs a gather/scatter bridge launch (2-4 us), and each mixed combination needs its own end-to-end self-check. That is a lot of new surface to build before we know which kernel is broken. Prepare-time per-kernel CUDA-event timing (now in the finite-fix review) gives the same 'time the healthy kernel' evidence without touching kernel_fn.
confounders: marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: the mixed path cannot share master's block_size_m=32 align at bs=256 with the wgmma block-16 layout without a second align or a detuned Marlin. Any mixed-path timing therefore changes the incumbent Marlin row it is compared against.
align-parallel-per-expert-verify: same align-bypass accounting as the sibling. With two aligns in a mixed path it doubles.
interference: No ab companion. The interference is with the sibling, which shares the bug: running both in parallel duplicates the localisation. Merge step (1) (independent per-kernel verdicts and PATH CHOSEN lines, with w2 fed Marlin's cache2) into finite-fix. Re-mint step (2) (per-kernel enable in kernel_fn with a bridge) as a stage-3 hypothesis only if finite-fix's compact summary shows one kernel at rel-L2 <= 1e-2 and the other not. At that point the bridge direction is known: gather cache2 into h_sorted if only w2 passes, scatter h_sorted into cache2 if only w13 passes.
rules_flags: None. If it is ever minted, the bridge launch and any second align are timed work and belong in the replaced-kernel sum.
open_questions: If finite-fix shows both kernels correct, this hypothesis is obsolete. Archive it instead of running it.

If finite-fix shows exactly one kernel correct, is the healthy kernel's prepare-time speed against Marlin (discounted 20-25%) good enough to justify the bridge cost? Decide that before minting stage 3.
